title: Cross-cancer direction and MTAG-borrowing explorer

definitions.DSI: sign agreement of a locus across the cancers in which it is genome-wide significant; +1 = all pairs concordant, -1 = all pairs antagonistic
definitions.borrowed: 1 - |z_own| / |z_MTAG|; the share of a cancer's MTAG estimate that is not present in that cancer's own GWAS. z-scores are stored to six decimals and the fraction is computed from the stored values, so the fraction reproduces the formula exactly when recomputed from the released file.
definitions.own_gwas_supports: the locus reaches genome-wide significance in at least two of its own, unborrowed GWAS

caveats: Direction classes are inferred from MTAG. In the discovery-panel reversed class every locus is a two-cancer locus, and the reversed-arm cancer never reaches genome-wide significance in its own GWAS (median borrowing 73.9-79.3%) while the concordant-arm cancer always does. Treat the reversed class as a model prediction, not as established biological antagonism.
Borrowing is not a defect of MTAG; it is what MTAG is for. It is reported so that a reader can see which estimates are observations and which are predictions.
A negative borrowed share means that cancer's own GWAS estimate exceeds its MTAG estimate: MTAG shrinks as well as amplifies.
Loci were selected for cross-cancer pleiotropy, so the excess of aligned loci is an upper bound on concordance, not an unbiased estimate; the reversed class shows no excess over the sign-flip null.
Effect sizes are on the standardised (z) scale and are not comparable across cancers with different sample sizes.

Significance flags are computed from the stored six-decimal z-scores; a value within 5e-7 of the genome-wide threshold can therefore differ from the flag in the manuscript tables, which use full precision.
source: public GWAS summary statistics; see the accompanying manuscript and code release
